title: 11/16/2026 | Kevin Kennedy | PL | Recusal of Chairman Gleeson, PUC Docket Nos. 59182 and 59475, and support of John B. Bradley's Motion for Conditional Disclosure on the Record and Conditional Recusal of Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson (docket item 6670)

=== jkk 59182-59475 Recusal letter (2026-11-16).pdf ===
November 16, 2026



Re: Recusal of Chairman Gleeson, PUC Docket Nos. 59182 and 59475


Dear Chairman Gleeson and Commissioners:

According to POLITICO, Governor Abbott’s Chief of Staff, Robert Black, led a meeting with the subject
“Transmission roundtable” on December 16, 2025. POLITCO has recently made available a copy of the
closed-door meeting’s confirmed stakeholder list, which included Chairman Gleeson, Oncor, AEP,
CenterPoint, ERCOT, Amazon, Google, META, Nvidia, and the Governor’s staff, among others. It is my
understanding POLITICO obtained the stakeholder list of the previously undisclosed meeting through a
Texas Public Information Request to the Governor’s Office.

This high-powered transmission line meeting was held six months after Oncor and LCRA held public
meetings for the Bell County East to Big Hill (59475) and Big Hill to Sand Lake 765-kV line (59182). It
was held just a few weeks before Oncor and LCRA TSC submitted their CCN application for 59182. It
was held after Oncor submitted its CCN application for Longshore to Drill Hole 765-kV line (59029).

The five 765-kV transmission line projects of the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP), spanning over
1,200 miles, are the first 765-kV in Texas and the first segments in a colossal, 4,000 to 5,000-mile bulk
765-kV bulk transmission proposal submitted by ERCOT and transmission companies that covers
virtually the entire State of Texas. The 765-kV lines are purported to be necessary due largely to the
explosion of ANTICIPATED data centers. We do not know exactly what was discussed but given the
attendees and the timing, it would seem wholly unreasonable to assume the PBRP 765-kV lines, including
Import Path 2, were not key points of discussion at this “Transmission roundtable”.

As such, I rightfully question the certainty of Chairman Gleeson’s impartiality and cite 16 TAC 22.3.f.1 in
requesting he recuse himself from any further matters and decisions on 59182 and 59475.

Further, I support John B. Bradley's Motion for Conditional Disclosure on the Record and Conditional
Recusal of Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson (docket item 6670).


Very truly yours,
Kevin Kennedy, P.E. (retired)

By: /s/ J. Kevin Kennedy

Pro se Intervenor: 59182 & 59475
630 County Road 282
Bertram, TX 78605
Telephone: (512) 639-1720
Email: jkkennedy.tx@gmail.com
